caseStudy.title: Property-document checker
caseStudy.summary: A legal workspace that helps surface issues in land documents before they become expensive problems.
caseStudy.meta: Product design · Stealth AI startup, legal-tech · Aug 2023 – Feb 2024

sections.title: Context
sections.body: The startup was building an AI product for the legal market in India. Designs from an earlier freelancer had been set aside, so I redesigned web and mobile from scratch. The founders had long feature lists, and I was the designer on this project.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: Checking a land document for problems can take a lawyer weeks. The idea was a checker that flags issues early, so a lawyer’s time goes to judgment instead of searching.

sections.title: Options
sections.body: The first big choice was one product or two. Leadership decided on two, a consumer legal marketplace and an AI workspace for lawyers, after talking with the founders’ network and with lawyer focus groups. I contributed to those discussions as the designer.

sections.title: What I cut
sections.body: The founders’ feature lists were long. I questioned them and cut scope down to the core jobs a lawyer needed done, so the first version could be built and tested.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body: The two apps launched on web and mobile with 1K+ downloads, mostly through the founders’ network. I don’t have usage numbers for the property-document checker itself. If I were measuring it, I’d look at how long a first review takes and how often a flagged issue turns out to be real.

sections.title: Background
sections.body: Univ.AI was an edtech company where Ivy League professors taught live to Indian learners, with a curriculum like a college’s. It needed its own platform to cut costs on third-party tools.

sections.title: My part
sections.body: As the UX/UI intern I audited the existing screens and built the platform’s first design system. I designed the learner flows (discovery, course pages, video, notes and community), a job portal with profiles, a recruiter side, applications and tracking, and a staff tool for teaching assistants inside the platform. I ran the interviews with the teaching assistants, with my mentor shadowing and stepping in when needed.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body: I handed the designs to engineering, and what shipped differed from what I had designed. I don’t have metrics for this work. The company later shut down after failing to raise funding.
